stories.title: The Jensen Huang Scandal Has Shocked Even Scandal-Prone Silicon Valley
stories.summary: The departure of Jensen Huang has surprised the tech industry. This event has led to discussions within the community about why highly successful individuals sometimes make poor decisions.

stories.title: What Went Wrong With Microsoft Global Outage: How The World Suffered With The Monstrous Disruption
stories.summary: A network capacity upgrade caused a significant global outage for Microsoft, affecting services like Outlook and Copilot. The company explained the cause of the disruption, the reasons for the extended recovery time, and the impact on businesses and users worldwide.

stories.title: A Maryland county used AI cameras on school buses to generate 375,000 tickets and $92 million in fines; i
stories.summary: A Maryland county utilized AI cameras on school buses, resulting in the issuance of 375,000 tickets and generating $92 million in fines.

stories.title: 'Radical Optimism': Ankiti Bose Sees AGI Transforming Science, Healthcare And Human Exploration
stories.summary: Ankiti Bose of Terra Invest believes that Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) has the potential to significantly advance scientific discovery, revolutionize healthcare, and enhance human capabilities. She also highlighted the importance of implementing safeguards alongside these advancements.

stories.title: Agnikul to set up an industrial unit in AP’s space city
stories.summary: Agnikul plans to establish an industrial unit in Andhra Pradesh's space city.

stories.title: Wall Street Loses a Powerful Dealmaker After Nvidia’s CEO Is Ousted
stories.summary: A significant figure in Wall Street's dealmaking scene has been removed from his position as CEO of Nvidia. This individual was known for his role in leading the development of artificial intelligence, a sector valued in the trillions.

stories.title: Edge For India? US Assures Comparative Tariff Advantage In Proposed Trade Deal, Says Report
stories.summary: Reports indicate that the United States has promised India a favorable tariff position compared to other countries in a potential trade agreement. This development comes as negotiations for the deal are reportedly nearing their conclusion.

stories.title: Wall Street's next bet: S&P 500 set to climb 14% despite slowing earnings growth - report
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs predicts that the S&P 500 will increase by over 14% in the coming year, reaching 8,700 points. This positive forecast is based on the idea that lower stock valuations could lead to good returns, even if company earnings grow more slowly.

stories.title: Anthropic IPO draws six times demand, but valuation remains under scrutiny
stories.summary: Anthropic's initial public offering has attracted six times the demand for shares, but concerns about its overall valuation persist.

stories.title: Sunil Mittal Calls for Rs 350 Monthly Mobile Tariffs, Says Current Rates Are Too Low
stories.summary: Sunil Mittal has advocated for an increase in India's average monthly mobile tariff to Rs 350. He argues that current rates are too low to cover rising operational costs and the necessary investments in telecommunications infrastructure.

stories.title: Trump to Meet With Putin and Xi in China, With Nuclear Proliferation on the Agenda
stories.summary: The president is scheduled to meet with the leaders of Russia and China in China. Discussions will focus on nuclear proliferation and the conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Jaishankar Says Bulk Of US-India Trade Deal Issues Resolved As America Hints At Tariff Advantage
stories.summary: Most issues regarding the trade agreement between the United States and India have been resolved, as the U.S. suggests a potential tariff advantage.

stories.title: 'India No Longer Democracy': Rahul Gandhi Attacks BJP-Led Regime In Hyderabad
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi stated in Hyderabad that India is no longer a democracy, criticizing the current BJP-led government.

stories.title: The Trump administration is diverting billions in health funding away from low-income countries, defying Congress’ plans
stories.summary: The Trump administration is reallocating billions of dollars in health funding, moving it away from low-income countries. This action goes against the plans set by Congress.

stories.title: Nvidia Scandal Prompts Questions of What It Means to Be a Spy
stories.summary: U.S. intelligence agencies suspect a woman involved with Jensen Huang was a Chinese asset. They are still investigating the full extent of her involvement and what it signifies for espionage.

stories.title: Trump administration warns of more H-1B, PERM suspensions for universities, companies
stories.summary: The Trump administration has indicated potential further suspensions of H-1B and PERM visas, which could impact universities and companies. This action suggests a tightening of immigration policies affecting skilled workers and foreign labor in the U.S.

stories.title: H-1B Visa Renewals May Face Fresh Scrutiny Under US Proposal
stories.summary: A new proposal in the U.S. may lead to increased scrutiny for H-1B visa renewals. This could make it more challenging for current H-1B visa holders to extend their stay in the country.

stories.title: IBM Makes a Major Visa Decision That Could Force Some Employees to Leave the US
stories.summary: IBM has made a significant decision regarding visas that might require some of its employees to leave the United States. This move could affect the company's workforce and operations in the U.S.

stories.title: Trump Admin Questions Microsoft’s H-1B Applications After Outage
stories.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly scrutinizing Microsoft's H-1B visa applications following a recent outage. This indicates a closer look at how companies utilize these visas, especially in the context of operational issues.

stories.title: Canada sets annual target of 150,000 new international students through 2029 | Hindustan Times
stories.summary: Canada plans to welcome 150,000 new international students annually until 2029. This initiative aims to increase the number of foreign students in the country over the next several years.
